column4: The sun cannot overtake the moon, night is not a forerunner of day, and all يَسْبَحُونَ in an orbit; one ayah joins swimming, racing precedence, and a divinely fixed order.
ٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ are the foremost first ones, followed by وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُم; the race's leaders and the train behind them appear together.
Moses says his people are عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى and that he hurried ahead; this exactly stages a leader, followers on his trace, and unequal positions in one moving line.
فَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ depicts people rushing in their predecessors' tracks, showing that energetic following can carry the train in the wrong direction.
تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ names love of what arrives quickly, the closest parallel to preferring the near life and mistaking the first arrival for the better goal.
وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ completes 75:20: the later thing is left behind while the immediately arriving thing is loved.
People love ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ and leave وَرَآءَهُمْ a heavy day; the ayah turns temporal priority into the section's literal front-and-behind arrangement.
وَٱلسَّـٰبِحَـٰتِ سَبْحًا is the Qur'anic oath explicitly activated by the source section's running/swimming sense of س ب ح.
فَٱلسَّـٰبِقَـٰتِ سَبْقًا immediately turns the swimmers of 79:3 into forerunners, making their motion a race with ordered positions.
وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا repeats the section's decisive act: putting the nearer life first.
وَلَلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ states in one line that what comes later is better than what comes first.
The magicians answer لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ and limit Pharaoh's power to هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا, reversing the choice made in 87:16.
وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ supplies 20:72's reason and closely matches the claim that the later good is better and more enduring.
The flower of ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا is set against وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ, joining the near attraction to what is better and longer-lasting.
Worldly provision is مَتَـٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا, while what is with God is خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ; this is the section's two-stage comparison almost verbatim.
What people receive is worldly enjoyment and adornment, whereas مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ; the visible first portion is not the lasting winner.
مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ gives the section's endurance claim as a direct contrast between exhaustion and remaining.
Guidance increases for the guided, and ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ are better in reward and return; it joins guidance, remaining, and the better destination.
ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ are better with the Lord than wealth and children, making the enduring entrant outrank the near life's adornments.
سَابِقُوٓا۟ directs the race toward forgiveness and a garden, relocating competitive speed from the passing world of 57:20 to the lasting goal.
ٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا and ٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ are the literal near and far banks named by the source section, spatializing its two temporal destinations.
وَٱلسَّـٰبِقُونَ ٱلسَّـٰبِقُونَ places the true foremost at the head of the final human ranks.
فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ ٱلْمُتَنَـٰفِسُونَ commands competition for the sealed drink of the blessed, identifying the lasting prize for which the race should be run.
وَٱلْعَـٰدِيَـٰتِ ضَبْحًا stages actual galloping, panting horses, the clearest Qur'anic realization of the section's running train.
ٱلصَّـٰفِنَـٰتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ are fine horses presented to Solomon, placing the section's animal image inside a test of attachment and remembrance.
Solomon's حُبَّ ٱلْخَيْرِ and ذِكْرِ رَبِّى are held in a deliberately difficult relation as the horses disappear, illuminating the boundary between created attraction and remembrance.
The returned horses' legs and أَعْنَاقِ are touched; their necks concretize the source dictionary's claim that a horse-train's guiding front can be its necks.
Birds in ranks each know صَلَاتَهُۥ وَتَسْبِيحَهُۥ; one ayah unites the two roots whose animal-motion senses build the section without replacing prayer or glorification.
At the call to prayer, believers must فَٱسْعَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ and leave trade; prayer, running toward remembrance, and setting aside the near gain meet in one command.
God records مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَـٰرَهُمْ, joining what people send ahead with the traces left behind them.
Moses and his servant turn back عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا, literally following their own tracks in reverse.
A people claim they are عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ; the ayah brings guidance and following traces together while exposing their mistaken equation.
The privileged repeat that they are عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ, making inherited tracks rather than truth determine who leads their line.
God knows ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ and ٱلْمُسْتَـْٔخِرِينَ, the ones advanced and the ones remaining behind in the human sequence.
The warning addresses whoever chooses أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ, turning moral response into advancing or falling behind.
وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ uses the same preference root for putting others ahead of oneself, a concrete ethical reversal of preferring the near life.
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ closely repeats the promise of being eased toward the easy course, now as the outcome of giving, fear, and truthfulness.
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ uses the same movement toward an end for the opposite course, showing that ease of progress does not by itself identify the good destination.
أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَـٰبِقُونَ joins hastening in good works to being their forerunners.
فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ makes differing directions converge in a race for good, giving the running image its proper object.
فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ again turns human difference into a race whose result is finally disclosed by God.
Joseph's brothers say إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ, an explicit human race whose reported sequence drives the scene.
وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ stages two people racing for the same door with opposed aims, showing that shared speed need not mean a shared moral course.
Among the heirs of the Book is سَابِقٌۢ بِٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ, the one who goes ahead through good deeds rather than mere temporal priority.
Whoever wants ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ may receive an accelerated share before being assigned Hell; immediate arrival is explicitly detached from final success.
Whoever wants the hereafter and سَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا directs striving toward its proper later goal.
The hereafter has أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَـٰتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا; after 17:18-19's two courses, the final ranking exceeds the preliminary one.
كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ states the exhaustion of every creature on earth, the first half of the section's passing-versus-remaining relation.
وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ completes 55:26 with what remains after every earthly entrant passes.
Each soul must inspect مَا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ, making present deeds provisions sent forward to tomorrow.
يَـٰلَيْتَنِى قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِى is the late realization that one should have sent something ahead for the life that truly counts.
نَكَالَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ places latter and former in one compact sequence inside the same surah as the swimmers and worldly preference.
Branded horses are among the beautified desires of ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا, while the good return is with God; the horse image itself becomes part of the near-life test.
Worldly life blooms like rain-fed growth and then becomes debris; its rapid course supplies the passing first stage from which 57:21 redirects the race.
Wealth and children must not distract from ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ; the ayah states the choice between near possessions and the remembrance that precedes prayer in the section.
أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِى directly joins prayer to remembrance, preserving the worship sense while the section hears a second horse behind it.
Guard all prayers and ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ; one prayer is explicitly located within an ordered series, echoing the positional sense developed for the prayer root.
The command to glorify before sunrise, before sunset, through the night, and at the day's edges lays تَسْبِيح along a temporal course with successive positions.
The night, day, sun, and moon each فِى فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ, directly realizing the source dictionary's stars swimming in their orbit.
فَٱلْجَـٰرِيَـٰتِ يُسْرًا depicts vessels or movers running smoothly, a Qur'anic counterpart to the source's animal with an easy, well-transferred gait.
وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَىٰهَا makes the moon follow the sun, a celestial version of the second runner immediately following the leader.
A person is told بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ, turning deeds into things placed ahead and left behind before the same surah contrasts immediate and later life.
Each soul learns مَا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ, the same front-and-back ordering applied to its own record.
A corrupt succession takes عَرَضَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ, while وَٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ; “the nearer/lower” makes the spatial root of worldly preference audible.
بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ says that God's remainder is better than fraudulent gain, joining “remaining” and “better” in a concrete commercial choice.
Moses leads a moving company on a dry path through the sea and is told not to fear دَرَكًا, being caught from behind; water, a track, and pursuit converge.
Pharaoh follows the departing company with his forces and the sea covers them, completing 20:77's front-and-rear pursuit.
وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُۥ وَمَا هَدَىٰ names the man at the head as a false guide, the reversal of a leading front that truly directs its followers.
A man comes مِنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ, running from the farthest edge toward the messengers' cause.
ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مَن لَّا يَسْـَٔلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ turns 36:20's runner into one who calls his people to follow the rightly guided.
ٱتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ explicitly aligns a follower behind a speaker who guides him on the sound road.
فَبِهُدَىٰهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ commands following the guidance of earlier prophets, joining direction with taking predecessors as one's lead.
Pharaoh's magicians ask to be أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ; the contest makes being first a deliberate tactic that does not win the encounter.
Moses is told to cast what is in his hand and it swallows their craft, supplying the result that overturns the first move of 20:65.
مَتَـٰعُ ٱلدُّنْيَا قَلِيلٌ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ makes the near stage brief and the later stage better.
The question أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ rebukes settling for the near life when its enjoyment is tiny beside the later one.
ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِبُّونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ precisely states the wrong preference between the two positions.
ٱسْتَحَبُّوا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ again identifies love of the nearer stage over the later one as the decisive error.
مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ divides one battle line by the two different goals its members put first.
ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ treats the wrong ordering as an exchange of the later life for the near one.
Worldly life is play and distraction, while وَلَلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ for the God-conscious; it restates which stage is truly better.
Those who do not expect the meeting with God رَضُوا۟ بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱطْمَأَنُّوا۟ بِهَا, concretely describing satisfaction with the first stage.
Whoever wants the worldly life and its adornment can be paid there in full, establishing the apparently successful early leg of the course.
For the people of 11:15 there is only fire in the hereafter, revealing why full payment at the first stage was not victory.
وَمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَـٰعٌ reduces the near life's apparent lead to a temporary provision when viewed from the later stage.
إِنَّمَا هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا مَتَـٰعٌ وَإِنَّ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ هِىَ دَارُ ٱلْقَرَارِ contrasts passing enjoyment with the settled abode.
The harvest of the hereafter grows, while one seeking the worldly harvest receives some of it and has no later share; two aims produce two finishes.
فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ opens the case whose defining choice is worldly preference in 79:38.
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ supplies the finish reached by the worldly preference of 79:38.
The opposing runner fears standing before his Lord and restrains desire, answering the preference described in 79:38.
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ supplies the other finish and completes the paired routes of 79:37-40.
Pharaoh's أَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ places a false claimant to “the highest” in the same surah as the swimmers and the preference for the near life.
Pharaoh boasts that his punishment is أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ; 20:73 answers the counterfeit claim to endurance with وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ.
The one meeting a good promise is contrasted with one merely furnished with worldly enjoyment and then brought to judgment, extending 28:60's better-and-lasting comparison.
Rain-fed worldly growth becomes dry fragments scattered by wind, providing the vanishing foreground against which 18:46 names the remaining good deeds.
أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ gives the destination and rank of the forerunners named in 56:10.
فِى جَنَّـٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ states where the foremost runners of 56:10-11 finish.
ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ places a large company of the former peoples within the foremost rank.
وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ adds the later company behind 56:13, continuing the first-and-later ordering inside the race passage.
The galloping animals strike sparks, continuing the bodily speed introduced in 100:1.
The runners raid at dawn, fixing the horse train's movement in a temporal sequence.
The horses raise a cloud of dust, showing the shared track and force of the moving company.
They penetrate the center of a gathered host, giving the running line an attained endpoint.
وَقَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم بِعِيسَى places Jesus after earlier prophets on their traces, a historical relay of leader and follower.
ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم بِرُسُلِنَا describes messengers following one another on predecessors' tracks.
The Prophet may consume himself عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم after people turn away, preserving the image of someone left behind at the tracks of those departing.
فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ makes safety depend on following divine guidance, aligning a follower behind the true guide.
فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ likewise joins following to guidance and promises the followers freedom from fear and grief.
As communities enter the Fire in succession, أُخْرَىٰهُمْ addresses أُولَىٰهُمْ; rear and front groups meet at the wrong finish.
أُولَىٰهُمْ answers أُخْرَىٰهُمْ, completing the exchange between the first and last groups in 7:38.
Those who spent and fought before the victory receive a greater rank than later participants, showing a case where morally costly precedence does affect final placement, though both receive good.
The rejecters argue that if revelation were good others would not have سَبَقُونَا إِلَيْهِ; their claim exposes the false assumption that social rank determines who may get ahead.
At an appointed term, a community can neither يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ nor يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ even an hour; temporal position is pictured as lagging or advancing.
When the appointed time arrives, people cannot fall behind or get ahead by an hour, a fixed finish no runner can alter.
مَّا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ makes a community unable either to outrun its term or trail it.
When the appointed term comes, people cannot move it backward or forward, applying the section's positional vocabulary to time.
مَا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ repeats the boundary that no collective can overtake its measured term.
The promised day cannot be delayed or advanced by an hour, fixing every entrant's place on the temporal course.
Whatever good people تُقَدِّمُوا۟ for themselves will be found with God خَيْرًا, making an act sent ahead become the better later possession.
Joseph orders that most of the early harvest be left in its ears, a concrete strategy of withholding present capacity for the later part of the course.
The hard years consume what was قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ except a guarded remainder, showing why spending the whole reserve at the beginning would fail.
God makes them leaders يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا, joining a place at the front with the act of guiding those behind.
Leaders from among the people يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا through patience, another explicit meeting of leadership and guidance.
Those who strive for God are promised لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا, joining sustained exertion to being directed onto the routes.
The servants of the Merciful يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا; their gentle gait is a nonlexical moral counterpart to the well-stepping animal in the source dictionary.
وَٱقْصِدْ فِى مَشْيِكَ commands a measured gait, making bodily step and moral measure coincide as they do in the section's easy-moving animal.
Prayer is established at the day's two ends and near portions of night, placing صَلَوٰة at successive positions on a temporal line.
Prayer runs from the sun's decline through nightfall to dawn recitation, again distributing worship across an ordered daily course.
فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ closes the surah that ranked the foremost, right, and left companies, joining the glorifying command to the race of final ranks.
Remembering the Lord morning and evening lays remembrance across the daily sequence immediately before 76:27 condemns love of the immediate life.
Night prostration and long glorification continue the ordered worship of 76:25 before the contrast with the immediately arriving life.
Abraham leaves a كَلِمَةًۢ بَاقِيَةً فِى عَقِبِهِ, a word remaining among those behind him in the generational line.
هُوَ ٱلْأَوَّلُ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرُ places God at both ends of the sequence, a boundary to applying the creaturely race's before-and-after to Him.
وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلْـَٔاخِرَةَ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ gathers the latter and former stages under God's ownership rather than the runner's preference.
فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ repeats that both ends of the sequence belong to God.
To God belongs praise فِى ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ, spanning the first and later lives rather than treating the first as self-sufficient.
وَسَارِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ directs speed toward forgiveness and the garden, a nonlexical race toward the enduring prize.
إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ describes a household whose haste is in good works, not in seizing the near life.
People emerge from graves سِرَاعًا as if racing to a marker, an afterlife rush that reverses the assumption that the only race is in the near life.
If God willed, people would race toward the path yet be unable to see it; speed without sight or guidance cannot secure the course.
ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ uses the source root in its concrete sense of drawing near, clarifying the spatial force heard inside ٱلدُّنْيَا.
فِىٓ أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ uses the same family for the nearest land, another literal spatial counterpart to “the near life.”
